title.narrative: Malawi Cholera Outbreak / Tropical Storm Freddy 2023

description.narrative:
Malawi is currently experiencing the worst Cholera outbreak in two decades, the first case was registered in Machinga district in the Southern region of Malawi on 2nd March 2022 and the Ministry of Health declared the cholera outbreak on 3rd March 2022. The cholera outbreak has now spread to Malawi’s northern and central regions, with the main risk factors being Wash Sanitation and Hygiene issues (WASH) such as unsafe water sources, open defecation, and poor food hygiene. There was a 95% increase in the number of cholera cases in November compared to October, and based on this the State President declared the 2022 cholera outbreak a ‘Public Health Emergency’. On 23rd January the Ministry of Health reported the case fatality rate to be 3.30%, which is over 3 times the normal acceptable threshold set by WHO of less than 1%. With approximately 11 million people at risk of Cholera in Malawi, the IFRC launched an Emergency Appeal on 23rd January 2023 requesting CHF 5.2 million, targeting 2.2 million people. This response will focus on Health Care and WASH activities to prevent and control the spread of the outbreak and reduce the mortality and morbidity rates through improved case management at the community level. The Swiss Red Cross will supply a Public Health for Cholera ERU. This ERU is fully staffed for the first wave, but the SRC may request support for second and third wave staffing, if this is necessary. IFRC has launched surge requests for several positions, for which the BRC surge team and register has appropriate profiles. Specifically, IFRC have requested a Regional Operations Coordinator, Public Health in Emergencies Coordinator, IM coordinator, and CEA Coordinator.
A DF application has been submitted which will provide BRC with the funds to finance surge delegates to support this response with 3 deployments of 3 months each. Which profiles BRC will support is still under discussion.

A total of 9,414 GBP to be sent to IFRC as allocation to support the Tropical Storm Freddy operation in Malawi that led to flooding and impacted communities. The overall goal of the appeal is to enable 160,000 people (32,000 households) affected by TC Freddy in five (5) affected districts (Blantyre, Chikwawa, Nsanje, Mulanje, and Phalombe) to meet their essential needs in a safe and dignified manner, recover from the crisis and strengthen their resilience to future shocks.
